questions.stem: Why is it light during the day?
questions.explanation: The light comes from the Sun. The sky looks blue precisely because sunlight scatters in the air.

questions.stem: What does a plant need in order to grow?
questions.explanation: From light, water and air a plant makes its own food. Soil mostly holds the roots and supplies salts.

questions.stem: Where does a puddle go after the rain when the sun comes out?
options: It rises whole to the sky
questions.explanation: The water evaporates into invisible vapour in the air. Later that vapour becomes rain again.

questions.stem: Why is winter colder than summer?
questions.explanation: In winter the rays graze the surface and warm it less. Distance to the Sun has almost nothing to do with it.

questions.stem: Ice floats in water. What does that tell us about it?
questions.explanation: Anything lighter than an equal volume of water floats. Water is unusual: it expands as it freezes.

questions.stem: What happens to a balloon if you take it out into the frost?
questions.explanation: In the cold the air inside takes up less room and the balloon sags. Back in the warm it puffs up again.

questions.stem: Why can we see the Moon if it does not shine by itself?
questions.explanation: The Moon acts as a mirror for sunlight. That is also why we see its phases.

questions.stem: You dissolved sugar in tea. Where did it go?
questions.explanation: The sugar did not vanish; it broke into tiny particles. The tea got heavier by exactly the sugar's weight.

questions.stem: Why is it harder to breathe in the mountains?
options: There is no oxygen at all
It is far too cold to breathe
The wind gets in the way
questions.explanation: Higher up each breath holds less air. Oxygen is still there, but a breath brings fewer molecules of it.

questions.stem: A hammer and a feather are dropped in a tube with no air. Which lands first?
questions.explanation: Without air, falling does not depend on mass. In a normal room it is the air that slows the feather.

questions.stem: Why do plants need carbon dioxide?
questions.explanation: From carbon dioxide and water, in light, a plant builds sugar and releases oxygen as waste.

questions.stem: A metal handle feels colder than a wooden one in the same room. Why?
options: It really is colder to touch
questions.explanation: Both are the same temperature. Metal simply pulls heat from your hand faster, and the hand reads that as cold.

questions.stem: Where does a tree's mass come from as it grows?
questions.explanation: Most of a tree is carbon taken from carbon dioxide. Soil supplies only a small share of the weight.

questions.stem: Why must you never put out burning oil with water?
options: Water is far too cold for that
Hot oil does not really burn
You can, it is an old myth
questions.explanation: Water is heavier than oil, boils instantly underneath it and throws burning droplets upward.

questions.stem: Antibiotics do not help with a common cold. Why not?
options: They are far too weak for it
People almost always take them wrong
questions.explanation: Antibiotics kill bacteria, and a virus is built differently. Against it they do nothing.

questions.stem: Why do astronauts float in orbit even though Earth's gravity reaches there?
options: There is no gravity up there
The heavy suits get in the way
In space they weigh very little
questions.explanation: The station and everyone in it fall around Earth at the same rate, so nobody feels any weight.

questions.stem: What do all living cells have in common?
questions.explanation: Every cell is separated from the world by a membrane and stores instructions in DNA. The rest varies.

questions.stem: Why do bacteria become resistant to antibiotics?
options: They get used to the drug
questions.explanation: No single bacterium changes. The ones that already had resistance survive and leave descendants.

questions.stem: What does it mean that energy is conserved?
options: It can be stockpiled for later
It cannot be spent at all
questions.explanation: Energy is neither created nor destroyed; it moves from one form to another, often into heat.

questions.stem: Why should one successful experiment not be trusted on its own?
questions.explanation: A single result can happen by luck. Science trusts what other people can repeat.
